source.text: Πολλοὶ οὖν ἐκ τῶν Ἰουδαίων, οἱ ἐλθόντες πρὸς τὴν Μαριὰμ καὶ θεασάμενοι ἃ ἐποίησεν, ἐπίστευσαν εἰς αὐτόν·

records.literal_gloss: Many therefore of the Jews, the [ones] having come to the Mary and having seen what he did, believed in him;

en.L: So many of the Jews, those who had come to Mary and had seen what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} did, believed in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: Many of the Jews who had come to Mary, and had seen what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} did, believed in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: Many of the Jews who had come to be with Mary saw what Jesus did, and they believed in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

es.L: Muchos, pues, de los judíos, los que habían venido a María y habían visto lo que hizo, creyeron en {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.
es.B: Muchos de los judíos que habían venido a ver a María, y que habían visto lo que hizo, creyeron en {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.
es.R: Muchos de los judíos que habían venido a acompañar a María vieron lo que hizo Jesús, y creyeron en {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.

fr.L: Beaucoup donc d’entre les Juifs, ceux qui étaient venus auprès de Marie et qui avaient vu ce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} avait fait, crurent en {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.
fr.B: Beaucoup de Juifs qui étaient venus auprès de Marie, et qui avaient vu ce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} avait fait, crurent en {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.
fr.R: Beaucoup de Juifs qui étaient venus tenir compagnie à Marie ont vu ce que Jésus avait fait, et ils ont cru en {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.

sw.L: Basi wengi wa Wayahudi, wale waliokuja kwa Mariamu na kuona alichofanya, walimwamini.
sw.B: Wayahudi wengi waliokuja kwa Mariamu, na kuona alichofanya, walimwamini.
sw.R: Wayahudi wengi waliokuja kuwa pamoja na Mariamu waliona alichofanya Yesu, wakamwamini.

decisions.choice: the Jews: the mourners from Jerusalem who had come to Mary and Martha
decisions.reason: These are the people John introduced in 11:19 and 11:31: Jews from Jerusalem, two miles away (11:18), who came to comfort the sisters after Lazarus died and followed Mary to the tomb (11:31-33). They are not the authorities, to whom some of them now go (verse 46), and not the people as a whole: Mary, Martha, Lazarus and Jesus himself are Jews. John names Mary because these visitors had been with her in the house and went with her to the tomb.

decisions.choice: those who had come ... and had seen: a description of the many who believed
alternatives: a selection: only some of those who came believed
decisions.reason: The words "those who had come" agree in form with "many", not with "the Jews", so they describe the believers: these many were the visitors who had seen the sign. Verse 46 then says that some of them went to the Pharisees, so not every visitor believed. The sentence does not say how many there were in all.

decisions.choice: seeing what Jesus did led them to believe in him
decisions.reason: The raising of Lazarus is the last and greatest of the signs John tells before the cross, and it does what the signs are written for: those who see it believe (2:11, 23; 20:30-31). Jesus had prayed at the tomb that the crowd standing by would believe that the Father sent him (11:42). Verse 46 shows the other response to the same sign.

decisions.choice: the Jews who had come to Mary (B); the Jews who had come to be with Mary (R)
decisions.reason: Here the word means the visitors in this scene (meaning decision m1). Balanced and Readable keep the word John wrote and tie it to the people present, as 10:19 does, so that no reader takes it to mean every Jew. No footnote is needed.

decisions.choice: Jesus; to be with; and they believed
decisions.reason: Readable names Jesus, says why the visitors had come (to keep the sisters company in their grief, 11:19, 31), and puts seeing and believing as two plain steps.

decisions.choice: los judíos (every level)
decisions.reason: Here the word means the mourners from Jerusalem in this scene (meaning decision m1), not the authorities, so no level says "dirigentes".

decisions.choice: narration in the passé simple (L, B); passé composé (R); speech in the passé composé at every level; the pluperfect for what had already happened ("avaient vu", "avaient donné")
alternatives: passé composé for narration at every level
decisions.reason: The French brief for the whole passage (11:45-57), as in 1:19. The passé simple ("crurent", "réunirent", "prophétisa") is the normal tense of written narrative and suits a public reading; Readable uses the passé composé ("ils ont cru"), the past tense French readers speak and learn first. The imperfect describes what went on over some days ("disaient", "cherchaient", 11:47, 56).

decisions.choice: les Juifs (L); beaucoup de Juifs qui étaient venus auprès de Marie (B, R)
decisions.reason: Here the word means the visitors from Jerusalem who had come to comfort the sisters (meaning decision m1), not the authorities, to whom some of them now go (verse 46). Balanced and Readable keep the word John wrote and tie it to the people present, as the English does; Mary, Martha, Lazarus and Jesus are Jews too.

source.text: τινὲς δὲ ἐξ αὐτῶν ἀπῆλθον πρὸς τοὺς Φαρισαίους καὶ εἶπαν αὐτοῖς ἃ ἐποίησεν Ἰησοῦς.

records.literal_gloss: Some however of them went away to the Pharisees and told them what did Jesus.

en.L: But some of them went away to the Pharisees and told them what Jesus had done.
en.B: Some of them, however, went off to the Pharisees and reported what Jesus had done.
en.R: But some of them went to the Pharisees and told them what Jesus had done.

es.L: Pero algunos de ellos fueron a los fariseos y les dijeron lo que Jesús había hecho.
es.B: Algunos de ellos, sin embargo, fueron a los fariseos y les informaron de lo que Jesús había hecho.
es.R: Pero algunos de ellos fueron a ver a los fariseos y les contaron lo que Jesús había hecho.

fr.L: Mais quelques-uns d’entre eux s’en allèrent vers les Pharisiens et leur dirent ce que Jésus avait fait.
fr.B: Certains d’entre eux, cependant, allèrent trouver les Pharisiens et leur rapportèrent ce que Jésus avait fait.
fr.R: Mais certains d’entre eux sont allés voir les Pharisiens et leur ont raconté ce que Jésus avait fait.

sw.L: Lakini baadhi yao walikwenda zao kwa Mafarisayo, wakawaambia mambo aliyofanya Yesu.
sw.B: Hata hivyo baadhi yao walikwenda kwa Mafarisayo, wakawaarifu mambo aliyofanya Yesu.
sw.R: Lakini baadhi yao walikwenda kwa Mafarisayo, wakawaambia mambo aliyofanya Yesu.

decisions.choice: some of them: some of the visitors from Jerusalem
alternatives: some of those who had just believed
decisions.reason: "Them" points back to the Jews who had come to Mary (verse 45). The word "but" sets these few against the many who believed, so they are most naturally visitors who did not believe.

decisions.choice: they went to report Jesus to the authorities
alternatives: they went in good faith, hoping to persuade the Pharisees
decisions.reason: John does not say why they went. The contrast with those who believed, and what follows at once (the council meets and plans his death, verses 47-53), show that their report worked against Jesus, as the healed man's report did in 5:15-16. Whatever their purpose, the effect was to bring the sign before his opponents.

decisions.choice: the Pharisees: the leading Pharisees in Jerusalem, who had a voice in the council
decisions.reason: The Pharisees were a movement devoted to keeping the law of Moses in detail. In John the Pharisees in Jerusalem act with the chief priests against Jesus (7:32, 45-48; 9:13-16), and in the next verse they gather the council together.

decisions.choice: reported
decisions.reason: "Reported" brings out that this was information carried to the authorities (meaning decision m2), without saying more about their motive than John does.

decisions.choice: les informaron
decisions.reason: As in English: information carried to the authorities (meaning decision m2).

source.text: συνήγαγον οὖν οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ Φαρισαῖοι συνέδριον, καὶ ἔλεγον· Τί ποιοῦμεν ὅτι οὗτος ὁ ἄνθρωπος πολλὰ ποιεῖ σημεῖα;

records.literal_gloss: Gathered therefore the chief priests and the Pharisees a council, and were saying, "What are we doing, because this the man many is doing signs?

en.L: So the chief priests and the Pharisees gathered a council, and they were saying, "What are we doing, since this man is doing many signs?
en.B: So the chief priests and the Pharisees called a meeting of the council. "What are we doing?" they said. "This man is doing many signs.
en.R: So the leading priests and the Pharisees called a meeting of the high council. "What are we doing about this man?" they asked. "He is doing many signs.

es.L: Reunieron, pues, los principales sacerdotes y los fariseos un concilio, y decían: «¿Qué hacemos, pues este hombre hace muchas señales?
es.B: Entonces los jefes de los sacerdotes y los fariseos convocaron una reunión del Consejo. «¿Qué estamos haciendo?», decían. «Este hombre está haciendo muchas señales.
es.R: Entonces los jefes de los sacerdotes y los fariseos llamaron a una reunión del Consejo Supremo. «¿Qué vamos a hacer con este hombre?», preguntaban. «Está haciendo muchas señales.

fr.L: Les chefs des prêtres et les Pharisiens réunirent donc un conseil, et ils disaient : « Que faisons-nous, puisque cet homme fait beaucoup de signes ?
fr.B: Les chefs des prêtres et les Pharisiens convoquèrent alors le conseil. « Que faisons-nous ? disaient-ils. Cet homme fait beaucoup de signes.
fr.R: Alors les chefs des prêtres et les Pharisiens ont réuni le grand conseil. « Qu’est-ce que nous faisons au sujet de cet homme ? demandaient-ils. Il fait beaucoup de signes.

sw.L: Basi wakuu wa makuhani na Mafarisayo wakakusanya baraza, wakawa wakisema, "Tunafanya nini, kwa kuwa mtu huyu anafanya ishara nyingi?
sw.B: Basi wakuu wa makuhani na Mafarisayo wakaitisha mkutano wa baraza. "Tunafanya nini?" wakasema. "Mtu huyu anafanya ishara nyingi.
sw.R: Basi viongozi wa makuhani na Mafarisayo wakaitisha mkutano wa baraza kuu. "Tufanye nini juu ya mtu huyu?" wakaulizana. "Anafanya ishara nyingi.

decisions.choice: a council: a meeting of the Sanhedrin, the high council in Jerusalem
decisions.reason: The word means a council or a session of one. Here it is the Sanhedrin, the highest Jewish council, which met in Jerusalem under the high priest and was made up of chief priests, elders and teachers of the law, among them Pharisees (compare Mark 14:53-55; Acts 5:21, 34). Under Roman rule it governed the affairs of the Jewish people in Judea. The word has no article, so John may mean that they called a session of it rather than naming the body; the council is the same either way.

decisions.choice: the chief priests and the Pharisees: the leaders who sat on the council
decisions.reason: As in 7:32 and 7:45, the chief priests (the high priest and the leading priestly families) and the Pharisees act together against Jesus. They do so again in verse 57 and at the arrest (18:3).

decisions.choice: What are we doing?: a complaint that they are doing nothing while he acts
alternatives: What are we to do?: asking for a plan
decisions.reason: The verb is present, "what are we doing", and the reason follows: this man is doing many signs. The two forms of the verb "do" are set side by side: he does signs, they do nothing. The question may also be asking what they should do, and Caiaphas answers that in verse 50; the sense comes to much the same.

decisions.choice: this man is doing many signs: the council admits the signs, and they do not lead it to believe
decisions.reason: The council does not deny that the signs are real. What leads many to believe in Jesus (verse 45) leads the council to plan his death (verse 53). John comes back to this at the close of Jesus's public work: though he had done so many signs before them, they did not believe in him (12:37). "This man" is how his opponents speak of him when they will not use his name (9:16, 24).

decisions.choice: two sentences with "they said" (B) or "they asked" (R) between them
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable set the question and the reason for it apart, as people speak, and Readable says what they were asking about. The leaders' words run on into verse 48.

decisions.choice: leading priests; the high council
decisions.reason: As in 7:45, Readable says "leading priests", which a young reader can follow, and "high council" to show which council is meant (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: los jefes de los sacerdotes; el Consejo (Supremo)
decisions.reason: As in John 7: plain words for the chief priests and the Sanhedrin (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: les chefs des prêtres (every level); un conseil (L), le conseil (B), le grand conseil (R)
decisions.reason: "Les grands prêtres" would suggest several high priests at once; "les chefs des prêtres" names the high priest and the leading priestly families (meaning decision m2) and is plain enough for Readable, so it is used at every level, as the shared choices for John set out. The council follows the English: Literal keeps the Greek without the article, and Readable says "grand conseil" to show which council is meant (m1).

source.text: ἐὰν ἀφῶμεν αὐτὸν οὕτως, πάντες πιστεύσουσιν εἰς αὐτόν, καὶ ἐλεύσονται οἱ Ῥωμαῖοι καὶ ἀροῦσιν ἡμῶν καὶ τὸν τόπον καὶ τὸ ἔθνος.

records.literal_gloss: If we let alone him thus, all will believe in him, and will come the Romans and will take away of us both the place and the nation."

en.L: If we let {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} [go on] like this, all will believe in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and the Romans will come and take away both our place and [our] nation."
en.B: If we leave {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} alone, everyone will end up believing in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. Then the Romans will come and take from us both our holy place and our nation."
en.R: If we let {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} keep on like this, everyone will believe in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. Then the Romans will come. They will take our temple and our nation away from us."

es.L: Si lo dejamos [seguir] así, todos creerán en {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, y vendrán los romanos y nos quitarán tanto el lugar como la nación».
es.B: Si lo dejamos seguir así, todos acabarán creyendo en {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}. Entonces vendrán los romanos y nos quitarán nuestro lugar santo y nuestra nación».
es.R: Si lo dejamos seguir así, todos van a creer en {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}. Entonces vendrán los romanos. Nos quitarán nuestro templo y nuestra nación».

fr.L: Si nous {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} laissons [faire] ainsi, tous croiront en {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, et les Romains viendront et nous enlèveront à la fois notre lieu et [notre] nation. »
fr.B: Si nous {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} laissons faire, tout le monde finira par croire en {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}. Alors les Romains viendront et nous enlèveront notre lieu saint et notre nation. »
fr.R: Si nous {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} laissons continuer comme ça, tout le monde va croire en {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}. Alors les Romains vont venir. Ils vont nous prendre notre temple et notre nation. »

sw.L: Tukimwacha [aendelee] hivi, wote watamwamini, na Warumi watakuja na kutuondolea mahali petu na taifa [letu] pia."
sw.B: Tukimwacha tu, kila mtu ataishia kumwamini. Kisha Warumi watakuja na kutunyang'anya mahali petu patakatifu na taifa letu pia."
sw.R: Tukimwacha aendelee hivi, kila mtu atamwamini. Kisha Warumi watakuja. Watatunyang'anya hekalu letu na taifa letu."

decisions.choice: the place: the temple, the holy place of the nation
alternatives: their place of power and position
decisions.reason: "The place" was a way of speaking of the temple, the place God chose for his name (Deuteronomy 12:5; 1 Kings 8:29; Jeremiah 7:14). In John the Samaritan woman speaks of Jerusalem as "the place where people must worship" (4:20), and Stephen is charged with speaking against "this holy place" and saying that Jesus would destroy it (Acts 6:13-14). The council's worry, though, is also for its own standing, and "our place" may mean their position as rulers. The temple is the more likely sense, but the other cannot be ruled out.

decisions.choice: the nation: the Jewish people as a people, with the measure of self-rule Rome allowed them
decisions.reason: The word is used of a nation as a political body. The council fears that Rome would end what freedom the Jewish people still had to govern their own affairs. Caiaphas takes up the same word in verse 50, and John in verses 51-52.

decisions.choice: the fear: a popular movement around Jesus would bring Roman force
decisions.reason: Judea was ruled by a Roman governor, and the council kept its place by keeping order. Crowds gathering around a worker of signs could look like the start of a revolt; after the feeding of the five thousand the people had wanted to make Jesus king by force (6:15). About forty years later, in AD 70, the Romans did destroy Jerusalem and the temple after a Jewish revolt, which John's first readers knew. The leaders' fear came true, though not in the way they reasoned.

decisions.choice: all will believe in him: an exaggeration from fear
decisions.reason: "All" is the leaders' alarm speaking, not a count. The Pharisees say the same in 12:19: "look, the world has gone after him".

decisions.choice: our holy place (B); our temple (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "place" most likely means (meaning decision m1). The footnote gives the other sense, the leaders' position of power.

decisions.choice: nuestro lugar santo (B); nuestro templo (R); el lugar (L)
decisions.reason: As in English: says what "the place" most likely means (meaning decision m1).

source.text: εἷς δέ τις ἐξ αὐτῶν Καϊάφας, ἀρχιερεὺς ὢν τοῦ ἐνιαυτοῦ ἐκείνου, εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Ὑμεῖς οὐκ οἴδατε οὐδέν, οὐδὲ λογίζεσθε ὅτι συμφέρει ὑμῖν ἵνα εἷς ἄνθρωπος ἀποθάνῃ ὑπὲρ τοῦ λαοῦ καὶ μὴ ὅλον τὸ ἔθνος ἀπόληται.

records.literal_gloss: One however certain of them, Caiaphas, high priest being of the year that, said to them, "You not know nothing, \v 50 nor consider that it is profitable for you that one man should die for the people and not whole the nation should perish."

en.L: But a certain one of them, Caiaphas, being high priest that year, said to them, "You do not know anything, \v 50 nor do you reckon that it is to your advantage that one man die for the people and the whole nation not perish."
en.B: One of them, Caiaphas, who was high priest that year, said to them, "You do not know anything! \v 50 You have not worked out that it is to your advantage to have one man die for the people, instead of the whole nation perishing."
en.R: One of them was Caiaphas, the high priest that year. He said to them, "You do not understand anything! \v 50 Think about it. It is better for you if one man dies for the people. Then the whole nation will not be destroyed."

es.L: Pero uno de ellos, Caifás, que era sumo sacerdote aquel año, les dijo: «{{plural_you:Ustedes no saben|Vosotros no sabéis}} nada, \v 50 ni {{plural_you:piensan|pensáis}} que {{plural_you:les|os}} conviene que un hombre muera por el pueblo y no que perezca toda la nación».
es.B: Uno de ellos, Caifás, que era sumo sacerdote aquel año, les dijo: «¡{{plural_you:Ustedes no saben|Vosotros no sabéis}} nada! \v 50 No {{plural_you:se dan|os dais}} cuenta de que {{plural_you:les|os}} conviene que un hombre muera por el pueblo, y no que perezca toda la nación».
es.R: Uno de ellos era Caifás, el sumo sacerdote de aquel año. Les dijo: «¡{{plural_you:Ustedes no entienden|Vosotros no entendéis}} nada! \v 50 {{plural_you:Piénsenlo|Pensadlo}} bien. Es mejor para {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} que un hombre muera por el pueblo. Así no será destruida toda la nación».

fr.L: Mais l’un d’eux, Caïphe, qui était grand prêtre cette année-là, leur dit : « Vous, vous ne savez rien, \v 50 et vous ne considérez pas qu’il est de votre intérêt qu’un seul homme meure pour le peuple et que la nation tout entière ne périsse pas. »
fr.B: L’un d’eux, Caïphe, qui était grand prêtre cette année-là, leur dit : « Vous ne savez rien du tout ! \v 50 Vous ne voyez pas qu’il est de votre intérêt qu’un seul homme meure pour le peuple, plutôt que de voir périr la nation tout entière. »
fr.R: L’un d’eux était Caïphe, le grand prêtre de cette année-là. Il leur a dit : « Vous ne comprenez rien ! \v 50 Réfléchissez. Il vaut mieux pour vous qu’un seul homme meure pour le peuple. Comme ça, la nation tout entière ne sera pas détruite. »

sw.L: Lakini mmoja wao, Kayafa, aliyekuwa kuhani mkuu mwaka ule, akawaambia, "Ninyi hamjui neno lolote, \v 50 wala hamhesabu kwamba ni faida kwenu mtu mmoja kufa kwa ajili ya watu, na taifa lote lisiangamie."
sw.B: Mmoja wao, Kayafa, aliyekuwa kuhani mkuu mwaka ule, akawaambia, "Ninyi hamjui chochote! \v 50 Hamjafikiri kwamba ni faida kwenu mtu mmoja afe kwa ajili ya watu, badala ya taifa zima kuangamia."
sw.R: Mmoja wao alikuwa Kayafa, kuhani mkuu wa mwaka ule. Akawaambia, "Hamwelewi chochote! \v 50 Fikirini. Ni afadhali kwenu mtu mmoja afe kwa ajili ya watu. Ndipo taifa zima halitaangamizwa."

decisions.choice: high priest that year: high priest in that fateful year, the year Jesus died
alternatives: the office changed hands every year
decisions.reason: Caiaphas was high priest from about AD 18 to 36, a long time for that office; the Romans appointed and removed high priests as they chose, and some served only a short time, but the office was not an annual one. "That year" marks the year of Jesus's death, the year in which the high priest's words carried more meaning than he knew. John repeats the phrase in verse 51 and in 18:13.

decisions.choice: You do not know anything: a blunt rebuke
decisions.reason: The Greek doubles the negative for force ("you do not know nothing"), and "you" is stressed. Caiaphas dismisses the others' worry as the talk of men who cannot see the obvious answer.

decisions.choice: one man should die for the people: on behalf of them, in their place
alternatives: for the people's sake only, without the sense of in their place
decisions.reason: The word "for" means on behalf of, and here also instead of: one man dies so that the nation does not. Caiaphas means a political calculation: hand one troublemaker over to death and spare the nation Rome's anger. John hears in the same words the meaning of Jesus's death, as the good shepherd who lays down his life for the sheep (10:11, 15), and says so in verses 51-52.

decisions.choice: the people and the whole nation: the same people, named in two ways
decisions.reason: "The people" is the word often used of Israel as God's people; "nation" is the word for a people as a political body, used in verse 48. Caiaphas uses both of the one people he means to save.

decisions.choice: for you (SBLGNT)
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts have "for us", as the King James Version reflects, and some leave the word out. The SBLGNT reads "for you", which keeps Caiaphas speaking down to the others. The sense of the saying is not changed. A reviewer should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: for the people (every level)
decisions.reason: Every level keeps the plain "for", which can mean both "for their benefit" and "in their place" (meaning decision m3), so that Caiaphas's words can carry the second meaning John draws out in verses 51-52, as "for the sheep" does in 10:11.

decisions.choice: Think about it; Then
alternatives: nor do you consider; and not
decisions.reason: Readable breaks the long sentence and says plainly how the two halves are linked: one man's death means the nation is spared.

decisions.choice: por el pueblo
decisions.reason: Every level keeps the plain "por", which can mean both "for their benefit" and "in their place" (meaning decision m3). Caiaphas speaks to the council, so the plural "you" takes the setting.

decisions.choice: pour le peuple (every level); le peuple ... la nation
decisions.reason: French "pour" carries both "for their good" and "in their place" (meaning decision m3), as the English "for" does, so Caiaphas's words can bear the meaning John draws out in verses 51-52; "à la place de" would say only the second. "Le peuple" and "la nation" keep the two Greek words apart (m4), with "nation" for the people as a political body, as in verse 48.

source.text: τοῦτο δὲ ἀφ’ ἑαυτοῦ οὐκ εἶπεν, ἀλλὰ ἀρχιερεὺς ὢν τοῦ ἐνιαυτοῦ ἐκείνου ἐπροφήτευσεν ὅτι ἔμελλεν Ἰησοῦς ἀποθνῄσκειν ὑπὲρ τοῦ ἔθνους, καὶ οὐχ ὑπὲρ τοῦ ἔθνους μόνον, ἀλλ’ ἵνα καὶ τὰ τέκνα τοῦ θεοῦ τὰ διεσκορπισμένα συναγάγῃ εἰς ἕν.

records.literal_gloss: This however from himself not he said, but high priest being of the year that he prophesied that was going Jesus to die for the nation, \v 52 and not for the nation only, but that also the children of the God the [ones] having been scattered he might gather into one.

en.L: Now he did not say this from himself, but being high priest that year he prophesied that Jesus was going to die for the nation, \v 52 and not for the nation only, but so that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} might also gather into one the scattered children of God.
en.B: Caiaphas did not say this on his own. Because he was high priest that year, he prophesied that Jesus was going to die for the nation, \v 52 and not for the nation alone, but also to bring God's scattered children together into one.
en.R: Caiaphas did not think of this by himself. He was high priest that year, so God used his words as a prophecy. His words meant that Jesus was going to die for the nation. \v 52 But Jesus would not die only for that nation. He would also die to bring together into one all of God's children who are scattered everywhere.

es.L: Pero esto no lo dijo de sí mismo, sino que, siendo sumo sacerdote aquel año, profetizó que Jesús iba a morir por la nación; \v 52 y no solamente por la nación, sino también para reunir en uno a los hijos de Dios que estaban dispersos.
es.B: Caifás no dijo esto por su cuenta. Como era sumo sacerdote aquel año, profetizó que Jesús iba a morir por la nación, \v 52 y no solo por la nación, sino también para reunir en uno a los hijos de Dios que estaban dispersos.
es.R: Caifás no pensó esto por sí mismo. Él era sumo sacerdote aquel año, así que Dios usó sus palabras como una profecía. Sus palabras querían decir que Jesús iba a morir por la nación. \v 52 Pero Jesús no iba a morir solo por esa nación. También iba a morir para reunir en uno a todos los hijos de Dios que estaban dispersos por todas partes.

fr.L: Or il ne dit pas cela de lui-même, mais, étant grand prêtre cette année-là, il prophétisa que Jésus allait mourir pour la nation, \v 52 et non pour la nation seulement, mais afin qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} rassemble aussi en un les enfants de Dieu dispersés.
fr.B: Caïphe ne dit pas cela de lui-même. Comme il était grand prêtre cette année-là, il prophétisa que Jésus allait mourir pour la nation, \v 52 et pas seulement pour la nation, mais aussi pour réunir en un seul peuple les enfants de Dieu dispersés.
fr.R: Caïphe n’a pas eu cette idée tout seul. Il était grand prêtre cette année-là, alors Dieu s’est servi de ses paroles comme d’une prophétie. Ses paroles voulaient dire que Jésus allait mourir pour la nation. \v 52 Mais Jésus n’allait pas mourir seulement pour cette nation. Il allait aussi mourir pour réunir en un seul peuple tous les enfants de Dieu qui sont dispersés partout.

sw.L: Basi hakusema haya kwa nafsi yake, bali kwa kuwa alikuwa kuhani mkuu mwaka ule alitabiri kwamba Yesu angekufa kwa ajili ya taifa, \v 52 wala si kwa ajili ya taifa tu, bali ili awakusanye pia pamoja kuwa kitu kimoja watoto wa Mungu waliotawanyika.
sw.B: Kayafa hakusema hivi kwa akili yake mwenyewe. Kwa kuwa alikuwa kuhani mkuu mwaka ule, alitabiri kwamba Yesu angekufa kwa ajili ya taifa, \v 52 wala si kwa ajili ya taifa peke yake, bali pia ili awakusanye pamoja kuwa kitu kimoja watoto wa Mungu waliotawanyika.
sw.R: Kayafa hakuwaza jambo hili mwenyewe. Alikuwa kuhani mkuu mwaka ule, kwa hiyo Mungu aliyatumia maneno yake kama unabii. Maneno yake yalimaanisha kwamba Yesu angekufa kwa ajili ya taifa. \v 52 Lakini Yesu hangekufa kwa ajili ya taifa hilo tu. Angekufa pia ili awakusanye pamoja kuwa kitu kimoja watoto wote wa Mungu waliotawanyika kila mahali.

decisions.choice: he prophesied: God spoke through Caiaphas's words because of his office, beyond what he meant
alternatives: Caiaphas knew the deeper meaning and spoke it on purpose
decisions.reason: "Not from himself" means the true meaning of the words did not come from Caiaphas. In Israel the high priest was the one through whom God's guidance was sought (Exodus 28:30; Numbers 27:21), and the Scriptures tell of God speaking through a man against his own purpose (Balaam, Numbers 23-24). John does not praise Caiaphas: he meant a political murder, and God made his words say something true about Jesus's death.

decisions.choice: being high priest: because he was high priest
decisions.reason: The phrase gives the reason he prophesied: it was by virtue of his office in that year, not because of who he was.

decisions.choice: die for the nation: die on behalf of the people, in their place
decisions.reason: John takes up Caiaphas's "for the people" (verse 50) in its deeper sense. Jesus lays down his life for his sheep (10:11, 15) and for his friends (15:13). The nation would be spared not by handing a man to Rome but by his dying for them.

decisions.choice: the scattered children of God: those from every nation who will believe in Jesus, gathered into one people
alternatives: the Jews scattered among the nations, gathered back to God's people
decisions.reason: In John the "children of God" are those who receive Jesus and believe in his name (1:12); here they are called so before they have come, as the "other sheep" are his before he brings them (10:16). The words recall God's promises to gather his scattered people from the ends of the earth (Isaiah 43:5-6; 49:5-6; Ezekiel 34:12; 37:21-22), promises made first to scattered Israel. Because "not for the nation only" sets them apart from the Jewish nation, people from the other nations are most likely meant (compare 12:20-32). The words could also mean Jews living among the nations, and the text does not settle it beyond doubt.

decisions.choice: gather into one: make one people of them
decisions.reason: "One" takes up the "one flock, one shepherd" of 10:16 and looks ahead to Jesus's prayer that those who believe may be one (17:20-23). The gathering is the purpose of his death.

decisions.choice: Caiaphas (B, R); God used his words as a prophecy; His words meant (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Caiaphas, so that the sentence is not taken to speak of Jesus. Readable says plainly what "not from himself ... he prophesied" implies, that God spoke through his words (meaning decision m1), and breaks the long sentence into short ones.

decisions.choice: Caifás; Dios usó sus palabras como una profecía (R)
decisions.reason: As in English: names Caiaphas, and Readable says how his words were a prophecy (meaning decision m1). "Sí mismo" is Caiaphas and has no setting; "hijos" includes daughters, as at 1:12.

decisions.choice: réunir en un seul peuple (B, R); rassembler en un (L)
decisions.reason: "Into one" means making one people of the scattered children of God (meaning decision m5). French "réunir en un" is hard to follow without a noun, so Balanced and Readable add "peuple"; Literal keeps the bare "en un". "Troupeau" would make the link with 10:16 plainer, but it would turn John's comment into a picture he does not use here.

source.text: ἀπ’ ἐκείνης οὖν τῆς ἡμέρας ἐβουλεύσαντο ἵνα ἀποκτείνωσιν αὐτόν.

records.literal_gloss: From that therefore the day they took counsel that they might kill him.

en.L: So from that day they took counsel that they might kill {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: So from that day on they plotted together to kill {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: From that day on, the leaders made plans to kill Jesus.

es.L: Así que, desde aquel día, acordaron matarlo.
es.B: Así que, desde aquel día, se pusieron de acuerdo para matarlo.
es.R: Desde aquel día, los dirigentes hicieron planes para matar a Jesús.

fr.L: À partir de ce jour-là donc, ils tinrent conseil afin de {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} tuer.
fr.B: Dès ce jour, ils complotèrent donc pour {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} faire mourir.
fr.R: À partir de ce jour-là, les chefs ont fait des plans pour tuer Jésus.

sw.L: Basi tangu siku ile walifanya shauri ili wamwue.
sw.B: Kwa hiyo tangu siku ile walifanya mipango pamoja ya kumwua.
sw.R: Tangu siku ile, viongozi walifanya mipango ya kumwua Yesu.

decisions.choice: took counsel: they deliberated together and settled on his death
alternatives: a passing wish to be rid of him
decisions.reason: The verb is used of taking counsel and coming to a decision. Before this, individuals and crowds had wanted to kill Jesus or tried to seize or stone him (5:18; 7:1, 30, 32; 8:59; 10:31, 39). Now the council itself makes his death its aim.

decisions.choice: from that day therefore: as a result of Caiaphas's advice
decisions.reason: "Therefore" ties the decision to Caiaphas's words. From that day, the question was not whether to kill Jesus but how and when (11:57; 12:10).

decisions.choice: the leaders; Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable names who made the plans and whom they meant to kill.

decisions.choice: los dirigentes; Jesús
decisions.reason: As in English: Readable names who made the plans and whom they meant to kill.

source.text: Ὁ οὖν Ἰησοῦς οὐκέτι παρρησίᾳ περιεπάτει ἐν τοῖς Ἰουδαίοις, ἀλλὰ ἀπῆλθεν ἐκεῖθεν εἰς τὴν χώραν ἐγγὺς τῆς ἐρήμου, εἰς Ἐφραὶμ λεγομένην πόλιν, κἀκεῖ ἔμεινεν μετὰ τῶν μαθητῶν.

records.literal_gloss: The therefore Jesus no longer openly was walking among the Jews, but went away from there into the region near the wilderness, to Ephraim called a town, and there he stayed with the disciples.

en.L: So Jesus was no longer going about openly among the Jews, but went away from there into the country near the wilderness, to a town called Ephraim, and there {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} stayed with the disciples.
en.B: So Jesus stopped moving about in public among the Jews of Judea. He left and went to the countryside near the wilderness, to a town called Ephraim, and stayed there with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples.
en.R: So Jesus no longer went around in public among the Jewish people of Judea. He left that area and went to a town called Ephraim, in the country near the wilderness. He stayed there with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples.

es.L: Por eso Jesús ya no andaba abiertamente entre los judíos, sino que se fue de allí a la región cercana al desierto, a una ciudad llamada Efraín, y allí se quedó con los discípulos.
es.B: Por eso Jesús dejó de andar en público entre los judíos de Judea. Se fue de allí a la región cercana al desierto, a un pueblo llamado Efraín, y se quedó allí con sus discípulos.
es.R: Así que Jesús ya no andaba en público entre la gente judía de Judea. Se fue de esa zona a un pueblo llamado Efraín, en la región cercana al desierto. Allí se quedó con sus discípulos.

fr.L: Jésus donc ne circulait plus ouvertement parmi les Juifs, mais s’en alla de là dans la région proche du désert, dans une ville appelée Éphraïm, et là {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} resta avec les disciples.
fr.B: Aussi Jésus cessa-t-il de circuler en public parmi les Juifs de Judée. Il partit de là pour la campagne proche du désert, dans une ville appelée Éphraïm, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} y resta avec {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples.
fr.R: Alors Jésus n’est plus allé en public parmi les Juifs de Judée. Il a quitté cette région et il est allé dans une ville appelée Éphraïm, dans la campagne près du désert. Il est resté là avec {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples.

sw.L: Basi Yesu hakuendelea tena kutembea waziwazi kati ya Wayahudi, bali alitoka huko akaenda katika nchi iliyo karibu na jangwa, katika mji uitwao Efraimu, naye akakaa huko pamoja na wanafunzi.
sw.B: Basi Yesu akaacha kutembea hadharani kati ya Wayahudi wa Uyahudi. Aliondoka akaenda katika nchi iliyo karibu na jangwa, katika mji uitwao Efraimu, akakaa huko pamoja na wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo Yesu hakuzunguka tena hadharani kati ya Wayahudi wa Uyahudi. Aliondoka eneo lile akaenda katika mji uitwao Efraimu, katika nchi iliyo karibu na jangwa. Akakaa huko pamoja na wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}.

decisions.choice: the Jews: the Jewish people of Judea, around Jerusalem, where the authorities had power
decisions.reason: Jesus does not leave the Jewish people: he goes with his disciples, who are Jews, to a town in the same land. He leaves the area around Jerusalem and Bethany, where the council could reach him. John spoke the same way in 7:1: Jesus would not go about in Judea because the Jews were seeking to kill him; and the disciples warned him in 11:8 about going back there. The word here means the people of that region, with the danger from their leaders in view.

decisions.choice: openly: in public, where all could see
decisions.reason: The word means openness, in speech or in action. Jesus had taught openly in the temple (7:26; 18:20). Now that the council has decided on his death, he no longer moves about in public until the hour comes for him to enter Jerusalem (12:12-13).

decisions.choice: Ephraim: a town near the wilderness; its site is not known for certain
decisions.reason: John gives only the name and that it lay near the wilderness, the dry and empty land of Judea. A place called Ephraim is mentioned in 2 Samuel 13:23, and 2 Chronicles 13:19 names a town Ephron or Ephraim. One possible site lies in the hill country some fifteen miles north of Jerusalem, at the edge of the wilderness, but this cannot be proved.

decisions.choice: the Jews of Judea (B); the Jewish people of Judea (R)
decisions.reason: The word means the people of the region around Jerusalem (meaning decision m1). Balanced and Readable keep the word John wrote and add where they were, so that no reader thinks Jesus left the Jewish people as a whole.

decisions.choice: in public; his disciples
decisions.reason: "In public" is the everyday phrase for this sense (meaning decision m2). English says "his disciples" where the Greek has the article.

decisions.choice: los judíos de Judea (B); la gente judía de Judea (R)
decisions.reason: The people of the region around Jerusalem (meaning decision m1); Jesus does not leave the Jewish people.

decisions.choice: abiertamente (L); en público (B, R); se quedó
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the word of 7:4 and 10:24; Balanced and Readable give its sense here (meaning decision m2). "Quedarse" for the ordinary sense of staying.

decisions.choice: les Juifs (L); les Juifs de Judée (B, R)
decisions.reason: Here the word means the people of the region around Jerusalem, where the council could reach him (meaning decision m1). Balanced and Readable keep the word John wrote and add where they were, as the English does, so that no reader thinks Jesus left the Jewish people as a whole: he goes with his disciples, who are Jews, to a town in the same land.

source.text: Ἦν δὲ ἐγγὺς τὸ πάσχα τῶν Ἰουδαίων, καὶ ἀνέβησαν πολλοὶ εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα ἐκ τῆς χώρας πρὸ τοῦ πάσχα ἵνα ἁγνίσωσιν ἑαυτούς.

records.literal_gloss: Was now near the Passover of the Jews, and went up many to Jerusalem out of the region before the Passover, that they might purify themselves.

en.L: Now the Passover of the Jews was near, and many went up to Jerusalem from the countryside before the Passover in order to purify themselves.
en.B: It was nearly time for the Jewish Passover. Many people from the countryside went up to Jerusalem before the festival to make themselves ritually clean.
en.R: It was almost time for the Jewish Passover festival. Many people from the country went up to Jerusalem early. They went to make themselves clean for the festival, as the law required.

es.L: Y estaba cerca la Pascua de los judíos, y muchos subieron del campo a Jerusalén antes de la Pascua para purificarse.
es.B: Se acercaba la Pascua judía. Mucha gente del campo subió a Jerusalén antes de la fiesta para purificarse según el rito.
es.R: Faltaba poco para la fiesta judía de la Pascua. Mucha gente del campo subió a Jerusalén con tiempo. Iban a purificarse para la fiesta, como mandaba la ley.

fr.L: Or la Pâque des Juifs était proche, et beaucoup montèrent de la région à Jérusalem avant la Pâque afin de se purifier.
fr.B: La Pâque juive approchait. Beaucoup de gens de la campagne montèrent à Jérusalem avant la fête pour se purifier selon le rite.
fr.R: C’était bientôt la fête juive de la Pâque. Beaucoup de gens de la campagne sont montés à Jérusalem en avance. Ils venaient se purifier pour la fête, comme la Loi le demandait.

sw.L: Basi Pasaka ya Wayahudi ilikuwa karibu, na wengi walipanda kwenda Yerusalemu kutoka shamba kabla ya Pasaka ili wajitakase.
sw.B: Ulikuwa umekaribia wakati wa Pasaka ya Kiyahudi. Watu wengi kutoka vijijini walipanda kwenda Yerusalemu kabla ya sikukuu ili wajitakase kwa desturi.
sw.R: Ulikuwa karibu wakati wa sikukuu ya Pasaka ya Wayahudi. Watu wengi kutoka vijijini walipanda kwenda Yerusalemu mapema. Walikwenda kujitakasa kwa ajili ya sikukuu, kama sheria ilivyotaka.

decisions.choice: the Jews: the Jewish people, whose festival it was
decisions.reason: As at 2:13 and 6:4, John names the festival as the people's, for readers who did not keep it. Jesus and his disciples kept it too.

decisions.choice: the Passover: the third Passover in John, at which Jesus dies
decisions.reason: John has mentioned Passover at 2:13 and 6:4. This one is the last: from here the Gospel moves toward it (12:1; 13:1), and Jesus dies as the Passover lambs are prepared (19:14, 36). Passover was one of the pilgrim festivals at which Israel came to Jerusalem (Deuteronomy 16:16).

decisions.choice: to purify themselves: to become ritually clean so as to keep the Passover
decisions.reason: Only those who were ritually clean could eat the Passover. Someone made unclean, for example by touching a dead body, had to be cleansed over seven days (Numbers 9:6-12; 19:11-19), so pilgrims came early. In Hezekiah's day many had eaten the Passover unclean, and the king prayed for them (2 Chronicles 30:17-20). Compare 18:28, where the leaders will not enter the governor's headquarters so as not to be defiled before eating the Passover.

decisions.choice: went up: the usual way of speaking of travel to Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Jerusalem stands high in the hill country, and pilgrims always "went up" to it (2:13; 5:1).

decisions.choice: the Jewish Passover
decisions.reason: Here the word means the Jewish people (meaning decision m1), so Balanced and Readable say "Jewish".

decisions.choice: make themselves ritually clean (B); make themselves clean for the festival, as the law required (R)
decisions.reason: "Purify" here means ritual cleansing, not washing dirt away; Balanced says "ritually clean", and Readable adds why it was needed (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: la Pascua judía
decisions.reason: The Jewish people, whose festival it was (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: según el rito (B); como mandaba la ley (R)
decisions.reason: As in English: ritual cleansing, not washing (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: juive (B, R); des Juifs (L)
decisions.reason: Here the word means the Jewish people, whose festival it was (meaning decision m1), so no level speaks of leaders; Balanced and Readable use the adjective, as in 2:13. Literal keeps the word John wrote.

source.text: ἐζήτουν οὖν τὸν Ἰησοῦν καὶ ἔλεγον μετ’ ἀλλήλων ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ ἑστηκότες· Τί δοκεῖ ὑμῖν;

records.literal_gloss: Were seeking therefore the Jesus and were saying with one another in the temple standing, "What does it seem to you?

en.L: So they kept seeking Jesus, and as they stood in the temple they were saying to one another, "What do you think?
en.B: They kept looking for Jesus, and as they stood in the temple courts they asked one another, "What do you think?
en.R: The people kept looking for Jesus. They stood around in the temple area and asked each other, "What do you think?

es.L: Buscaban, pues, a Jesús, y estando en el templo se decían unos a otros: «¿Qué {{plural_you:les|os}} parece?
es.B: Seguían buscando a Jesús, y mientras estaban en los atrios del templo se preguntaban unos a otros: «¿Qué {{plural_you:les|os}} parece?
es.R: La gente seguía buscando a Jesús. Estaban en el patio del templo y se preguntaban unos a otros: «¿Qué {{plural_you:piensan|pensáis}}?

fr.L: Ils cherchaient donc Jésus, et ils se disaient les uns aux autres, debout dans le temple : « Que vous en semble ?
fr.B: Ils cherchaient Jésus, et, debout dans la cour du temple, ils se demandaient les uns aux autres : « Qu’en pensez-vous ?
fr.R: Les gens cherchaient Jésus. Ils se tenaient dans la cour du temple et se demandaient les uns aux autres : « Qu’est-ce que vous en pensez ?

sw.L: Basi walikuwa wakimtafuta Yesu, na walipokuwa wamesimama hekaluni walikuwa wakiambiana, "Mnaonaje?
sw.B: Waliendelea kumtafuta Yesu, na walipokuwa wamesimama katika nyua za hekalu waliulizana, "Mnaonaje?
sw.R: Watu waliendelea kumtafuta Yesu. Walisimama katika uwanja wa hekalu wakaulizana, "Mnaonaje?

decisions.choice: they: the pilgrims who had come up early (verse 55)
decisions.reason: The subject of the verbs is the "many" who went up to Jerusalem before the festival. They are curious about Jesus, and the order of verse 57 explains why they wonder whether he will dare to come.

decisions.choice: were seeking ... were saying: going on over some days
decisions.reason: Both verbs are imperfect: the pilgrims went on looking for Jesus and talking about him in the days before the festival, as the crowds had at Tabernacles (7:11-13).

decisions.choice: What does it seem to you?: What do you think?
decisions.reason: The Greek idiom asks for an opinion.

decisions.choice: temple courts (B); temple area (R)
decisions.reason: The word means the whole temple area, with its courts, not the sanctuary itself (see the book's terms).

decisions.choice: The people
decisions.reason: Readable says who was looking for Jesus (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: los atrios del templo (B); el patio del templo (R)
decisions.reason: The 2:14 choice for the whole temple area.

source.text: ὅτι οὐ μὴ ἔλθῃ εἰς τὴν ἑορτήν;

records.literal_gloss: That not not he will come to the feast?"

en.L: That {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will by no means come to the feast?"
en.B: Will {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} not come to the festival at all?"
en.R: Do you think {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will stay away from the festival?"

es.L: ¿Que de ningún modo vendrá a la fiesta?».
es.R: ¿{{plural_you:Creen|Creéis}} que no va a venir a la fiesta?».

fr.L: Qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} ne viendra sûrement pas à la fête ? »
fr.B: Ne viendra-t-{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} donc pas du tout à la fête ? »
fr.R: Est-ce que vous pensez qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} ne va pas venir à la fête ? »

decisions.choice: a second question, as the SBLGNT punctuates
alternatives: one question: "What do you think, that he will not come to the feast?"
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT closes the first question after "What do you think?" and makes this a second one. The words could also be read as one question in which this clause says what they think. The sense is the same either way: they wonder aloud whether he will stay away.

decisions.choice: will by no means come: a strong denial, put as a question
decisions.reason: The Greek uses two negatives together, the strongest way of saying "not". The question leans toward the answer that he will certainly not come, given the danger (verse 57). Yet he does come (12:1, 12).

decisions.choice: the feast: the Passover
decisions.reason: The feast is the Passover named in verse 55.

decisions.choice: Will he not come ... at all? (B); Do you think he will stay away? (R)
alternatives: That he will by no means come? (Literal)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable turn the clause into an ordinary English question and keep its leaning toward "he will not come". "Festival" is the everyday word for the feast.

decisions.choice: ¿No vendrá ...? (B); ¿Creen que no va a venir ...? (R)
decisions.reason: As in English: an ordinary question that keeps its leaning (meaning decision m2).

source.text: δεδώκεισαν δὲ οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ Φαρισαῖοι ἐντολὰς ἵνα ἐάν τις γνῷ ποῦ ἐστιν μηνύσῃ, ὅπως πιάσωσιν αὐτόν.

records.literal_gloss: Had given now the chief priests and the Pharisees commands that if anyone should know where he is he should report, so that they might seize him.

en.L: Now the chief priests and the Pharisees had given orders that if anyone knew where {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was, {{gender:that person|he}} should report it, so that they might seize {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: Meanwhile the chief priests and the Pharisees had given orders that anyone who knew where Jesus was must report it, so that they could arrest {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: The leading priests and the Pharisees had given an order. Anyone who knew where Jesus was had to tell them, so that they could arrest {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

es.L: Y los principales sacerdotes y los fariseos habían dado órdenes de que, si alguno sabía dónde estaba, lo denunciara, para prenderlo.
es.B: Mientras tanto, los jefes de los sacerdotes y los fariseos habían dado órdenes de que cualquiera que supiera dónde estaba Jesús lo denunciara, para poder arrestarlo.
es.R: Los jefes de los sacerdotes y los fariseos habían dado una orden. Cualquiera que supiera dónde estaba Jesús tenía que avisarles, para que pudieran arrestarlo.

fr.L: Or les chefs des prêtres et les Pharisiens avaient donné des ordres pour que quiconque saurait où {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} était le fasse savoir, afin qu’ils puissent {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} saisir.
fr.B: Entre-temps, les chefs des prêtres et les Pharisiens avaient ordonné que quiconque savait où était Jésus le signale, afin qu’ils puissent {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}arrêter.
fr.R: Les chefs des prêtres et les Pharisiens avaient donné un ordre : toute personne qui savait où était Jésus devait venir le leur dire, pour qu’ils puissent {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}arrêter.

sw.L: Basi wakuu wa makuhani na Mafarisayo walikuwa wametoa amri kwamba mtu yeyote akijua alipo, aseme, ili wamkamate.
sw.B: Wakati huo wakuu wa makuhani na Mafarisayo walikuwa wametoa amri kwamba yeyote anayejua alipo Yesu lazima aseme, ili wamkamate.
sw.R: Viongozi wa makuhani na Mafarisayo walikuwa wametoa amri. Yeyote aliyejua alipo Yesu alipaswa kuwaambia, ili waweze kumkamata.

decisions.choice: had given orders: already given, before the pilgrims' talk
decisions.reason: The verb is pluperfect: the order was already out. This is why the pilgrims wonder whether Jesus will dare to come (verse 56).

decisions.choice: report: inform the authorities
decisions.reason: The verb means to make known, often of information laid before officials. Anyone who knew where Jesus was staying was to tell the chief priests and Pharisees. In the end it is Judas who leads them to him (18:2-3).

decisions.choice: anyone ... should report: any person at all, man or woman
decisions.reason: "Anyone" is not limited to men; the verb that follows has the same person as its subject.

decisions.choice: that person (default); he (traditional)
decisions.reason: The Greek has no separate pronoun here; the subject of "report" is "anyone" (meaning decision m3). The default says "that person", which is clear and does not suggest a man only; the traditional setting gives "he". Balanced and Readable need no pronoun.

decisions.choice: Jesus; arrest
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Jesus, since the chief priests and the Pharisees are the last people named, and say "arrest", the plain word for seizing someone by order of the authorities.

decisions.choice: no gender setting
decisions.reason: "Si alguno sabía ... lo denunciara" needs no separate pronoun in Spanish (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: quiconque (L, B); toute personne qui (R), with no gender setting
alternatives: si quelqu’un savait où il était, {{gender:cette personne|il}} devait le signaler
decisions.reason: "Anyone" means any person, man or woman (meaning decision m3). English needs the gender setting for the pronoun after "if anyone"; French can say "quiconque" or "toute personne qui", which are already inclusive and need no pronoun, so no setting is needed. This also keeps a second "il" out of a sentence whose "il" is Jesus.
